title: Never changing men in the band
summary: He has kept his band together for fifty years and says a band that stays together plays better because everyone knows their part.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You see, you man, you see, you see, man, you've been playing with me so long, and people ask me them things. You know, a man asked me that third night when I was older. He said, how long you been having a band? I said, man, I've been having a band for 50 years. He said, all the same men? I said, no. I said, a lot of my men died of him. I said, look, I don't, he said, you'll never change a man in your band. I said, no, unless he dies. I said, I don't change nobody. I don't never change a man, you know what I mean? A man, in a band, and that's the worst thing to do. If you got a band, and if you can hold that band together, you'll have a better band. You know what I mean? Because look, everybody knows what they got to do when they get on the job. You don't have to be telling this, this, and all that, you know what I mean? See, you make a better band. And a lot of people, now you take a lot of people come there at the Prairie Bridge, don't take them people who know what music you know. I've tried to tell people what bands play, they say, look, that band is not together. You understand what I'm talking about?

Well you see, if you've got to organize a band, it's band together. You know what I'm talking about? You see? That's why I don't never change a man to my band. See, man, it's been so long, but man, man, you're the oldest of him in Saturday, the oldest of the band. Yeah, you see? Yeah, you see?
